tldr: Foundry previews now let teams cap model and agent spending and centrally govern hosted-agent outbound destinations—useful controls to test before putting agents into production.
Azure AI Search and Foundry IQ can now honor Azure Storage permissions, enabling search results to reflect each user's access instead of relying on a separate access-control layer.
Anthropic has added Skills and long-running task support to Claude's MCP capabilities, while DoorDash reports 10× dispatch throughput and over 99.99% peak availability after a distributed redesign.

top.title: Foundry previews spending limits for models and agents
top.summary: Foundry cost controls let teams set a spending or token budget for a resource or project, then send an Event Grid alert or block new requests when usage reaches the configured threshold.
top.why: Test these controls against your usage patterns to decide whether project-level budgets can prevent unexpected model and agent spend.

top.title: Azure AI Search can enforce Azure Storage permissions
top.summary: Azure AI Search and Foundry IQ can now use supported Azure Storage permissions so search results are filtered according to each user's access.
top.why: Revisit your retrieval design: this can reduce the need to build and maintain a separate permissions-filtering layer for search results.

top.title: Foundry previews policy controls for hosted-agent outbound traffic
top.summary: Administrators can use Azure Policy to govern the outbound destinations of hosted agents; agent authors attach a compliant egress policy before creating an agent version.
top.why: Evaluate this for production agents that need controlled network access, rather than relying only on each author to restrict destinations.

top.title: Azure VMs can restrict which processes request managed identity tokens
top.summary: The generally available Metadata Security Protocol adds authentication and authorization for IMDS and Azure WireServer, addressing which processes inside a VM can request managed-identity tokens.
top.why: Review VM identity exposure and assess whether to enable the protocol so a compromised process has fewer paths to obtain an application's Azure credentials.

top.title: Site Recovery adds zonal DR for Ultra disks
top.summary: Azure Site Recovery now supports Zone-to-Zone disaster recovery for Ultra disks, allowing performance-intensive VMs to be replicated and recovered in another availability zone.
top.why: Reassess zonal recovery plans for critical Ultra-disk workloads that previously lacked this Site Recovery option.

also.title: Foundry previews routing MCP tool traffic through your gateway
also.summary: Foundry Agent Service can route MCP tool traffic through an organization's existing AI Gateway or Azure API Management endpoints.

also.title: Foundry previews native A2A passthrough for hosted agents
also.summary: Hosted agents can now forward native Agent2Agent requests directly, avoiding the previous conversion to the Responses protocol.

also.title: Windows Remote Recovery for Azure VMs enters public preview
also.summary: The preview adds Windows Recovery Environment access for VMs that cannot start, with Quick Machine Recovery and customer-authored remediations.

also.title: VMSS Uniform periodic update assessment enters preview
also.summary: Azure Update Manager can assess Uniform VM scale sets every 24 hours and publish compliance results to Azure Resource Graph.

top.title: Benchmark finds leading AI agents still struggle with everyday tasks
top.summary: A new benchmark finds that even advanced models struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely, sometimes creating new problems while attempting them.
top.why: Keep human confirmation and bounded permissions in workflows where an agent can take consequential actions; strong model performance alone is not evidence of dependable execution.

top.title: Walmart lets Meta's Muse agent shop Black Friday deals
top.summary: Walmart is making Black Friday deals available to customers shopping through Muse, Meta's AI agent.
top.why: Treat agent-led shopping as a live commerce channel and account for how product discovery and purchasing may move outside a retailer's own app.

top.title: Reports describe internal debate over releasing advanced AI models
top.summary: A report citing more than two dozen sources says employees at Anthropic and OpenAI have raised concerns internally about the risks of releasing advanced reasoning models.
top.why: Factor possible safety reviews or release restrictions into plans that depend on getting a particular frontier model or version.

also.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly discuss allowing Muse to shop on Amazon
also.summary: The companies are reportedly discussing ending Amazon's two-month blockade of Muse, with negotiations involving product recommendations and Amazon's advertising revenue.

also.title: Anthropic says Claude can create desktop apps from a prompt
also.summary: Anthropic added a capability for Claude to create functional Windows and Mac desktop applications from a single prompt.

top.title: Claude adds Skills over MCP and support for long-running tasks
top.summary: Anthropic's MCP update adds support for Skills and long-running tasks in Claude, extending how it can use external capabilities and handle work that does not finish in a single interaction.
top.why: Review your MCP integrations and agent workflows to see whether these capabilities can simplify task handling or reduce custom orchestration.

top.title: DoorDash redesign delivers 10× dispatch throughput
top.summary: DoorDash replaced a monolithic dispatch optimizer with a distributed design that separates coordination from computation, reporting 10× higher throughput and more than 99.99% peak availability.
top.why: Use the case study when evaluating whether a high-volume inference or optimization service should separate coordination from compute to scale and fail more independently.

top.title: Claude Ship targets the pull-request bottleneck from AI coding
top.summary: Anthropic's Claude Ship is aimed at automating approvals and addressing the pull-request bottleneck created as AI coding agents produce more code.
top.why: If coding agents are increasing review queues, evaluate whether this addresses your specific approval bottleneck before adding another step to your delivery process.

also.title: Confluent discarded its AI-assisted Kafka client rewrite after three months
also.summary: Confluent spent nearly three months using AI agents to translate Kafka's Java client into Rust, then discarded the work and started over.

also.title: Teleport argues agents should use delegated identity, not SSH keys
also.summary: The article describes giving an AI agent scoped, delegated access to operational resources such as Kubernetes logs instead of handing it a developer's SSH keys.

also.title: OpenAI uses Codex agents for difficult Spark upgrade work
also.summary: At QCon, an OpenAI engineering manager described using agents for open-ended operational tasks such as upgrading Spark, rather than trying to automate the entire data platform.
